etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English naval, from Middle French naval, from Latin nāvālis; equivalent to navy +‎ -al.

definitions.definition: (nautical) Of or relating to a navy.

quote.citation: 2012 March, William E. Carter, Merri Sue Carter, “The British Longitude Act Reconsidered”, in American Scientist‎[1], volume 100, number 2, page 87:
quote.text: Conditions were horrendous aboard most British naval vessels at the time. Scurvy and other diseases ran rampant, killing more seamen each year than all other causes combined, including combat.

definitions.definition: (nautical) Of or relating to ships in general.
